ai.name: xAI
ai.hook: Grok 4.5 ships as a 1.5T-parameter coding model priced for volume, not benchmark bragging rights.
insights: **$2/1M input, $6/1M output tokens**, with cache-hit discounts, 3x the parameter count of Grok 4.3
**Cursor** co-trained the model and calls it their most powerful yet
Context window expected back at **1M tokens** soon, Musk pitches it as 'Opus-class but faster'
ai.for_you: Watch the price point specifically, if Grok 4.5 API pricing holds, it's a cheaper backbone option for agency client work than Claude or GPT, worth a cost test against your current stack before committing to a vendor for the next SMB build.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Biggest model launch of the week, already covered yesterday but pricing/Cursor detail is new and directly actionable

video.title: xAI's Grok Code Fast One: Can It Beat AI Coding Rivals? #shorts

ai.name: OpenAI
ai.hook: ChatGPT voice mode finally gets a real upgrade, quietly delegates hard questions mid-conversation.
insights: New voice model routes complex queries to **GPT-5.5** behind the scenes and returns the answer without breaking flow
718 points, 481 comments on HN, the single biggest discussion of the week
Simon Willison had preview access for weeks and calls it 'very impressive'
ai.for_you: This delegation pattern (fast conversational layer + silent handoff to a bigger model) is exactly the architecture worth stealing for a yoga platform voice assistant, students ask casual questions fast, harder queries get routed to a stronger model without them noticing the seam.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Top HN story of the day, direct architecture pattern relevant to Pedro's builds

ai.name: Cognition

ai.for_you: Another data point that coding-model competition is compressing prices fast, good news for margin on the AI agency if you're billing SMBs for AI-assisted dev work, your input costs keep dropping while your rates don't have to.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Notable frontier coding model claim with real HN traction

ai.name: Noma Security
ai.hook: Researchers tricked GitHub's AI coding agent into leaking private repo contents.
insights: Called the exploit 'GitLost', 521 points and 196 comments on HN
Attack works through prompt injection embedded in seemingly normal repo content
ai.for_you: If you ever wire an AI coding agent into client repos for the agency, this is the exact failure mode to test for before you touch anyone's private codebase, run this exploit against your own setup first.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: High-engagement security story directly relevant to anyone deploying coding agents on client data

video.title: GitLost: How We Tricked GitHub’s AI Agent into Leaking Private Repos — Explained in 60s

ai.name: Craig Mod
ai.hook: Cut his newsletter tool bill from $7,000/year to $150 by rebuilding it himself with AI.
insights: Rebuilt Campaign Monitor equivalent, plus a private Twitter alternative called 'The Good Place' for members
Calls it the start of a 'golden age of tool building', anyone can now build software suited to their exact needs
Still refuses to use AI to actually write his prose, keeps AI as research assistant only
ai.for_you: This is literally your agency's pitch to PT SMBs made concrete, a solo non-developer replacing a $7K/year SaaS subscription with a custom AI-built tool costing $150. Use this exact story as a sales anecdote when pitching prospects on why custom AI tooling beats another subscription.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most concrete, swap-test-passing story of the day for the agency pitch

ai.name: Alec Collon
ai.hook: 347 points, 282 comments on a post about burning out from constant LLM use.
insights: High comment-to-point ratio suggests strong disagreement/discussion, not just agreement
Comes the same week as Craig Mod's counter-narrative about a 'golden age of tool building'
ai.for_you: Worth a skim as a gut-check, if you notice fatigue building AI agency work day after day, you're not alone, the tension between hype and burnout is a live debate right now, not just your own experience.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: High engagement, useful counterweight to daily AI hype

build_this.name: Flint
build_this.what_it_is: A visualization language specifically for AI agent outputs, lets agents render charts/diagrams instead of just text.
build_this.why_try_it: Directly usable for the agency, if you're building dashboards or reports for SMB clients where an agent summarizes data, Flint gives you a way to make agent output look like a real deliverable instead of a wall of text. Worth a quick prototype against one client's reporting need this week.

build_this.name: GeoSQL
build_this.what_it_is: A Claude/Codex skill that lets coding agents query and reason over geospatial data.
build_this.why_try_it: If any SMB client is retail, logistics, or real estate, a location-aware agent skill could be a quick differentiator, worth a 30-minute test to see if it plugs into a Claude Code workflow you already run.

build_this.name: OpenAI's coding eval methodology
build_this.source: OpenAI blog, via Hacker News (222 pts)
build_this.what_it_is: A framework for separating real signal from noise when benchmarking coding models.
build_this.why_try_it: Before you commit the agency's stack to Grok 4.5 or SWE-1.7 based on marketing claims, use this methodology to build your own 3-task eval against real client work, cheap insurance before switching vendors.

podcasts.episode: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice
podcasts.takeaway: Craig Mod replaced a $7K/year SaaS tool with a $150 AI-built custom one, and draws a hard line at using AI to actually write.
key_points: Rebuilt his newsletter sending infrastructure and Quicken-style tax tool himself with AI assistance
Built 'The Good Place', a private Twitter alternative just for his newsletter members
Keeps a tech-free zone in the mornings for deep thinking, resists 'mainlining' AI into every task
podcasts.for_you: The cost-replacement story ($7K to $150) is a ready-made case study to pitch PT SMBs who are paying for bloated SaaS subscriptions they don't need, position the agency as the team that builds the $150 version.

video.title: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice

podcasts.episode: The 100,000 Sandbox Problem, Akshat Bubna, Modal CTO
podcasts.takeaway: Modal is shifting from developer experience to agent experience, because production agents need hard guardrails and massive burst compute, not just good APIs.
key_points: RL rollouts can require 100,000 sandboxes running simultaneously
Kubernetes wasn't designed for bursty, compute-heavy agent workloads
Observability now matters more than reading the code agents produce
podcasts.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, this is infra-scale territory well beyond a solo agency's needs right now, but the observability-over-code-review point is worth remembering as your own agent workflows grow.

video.title: The 100,000 Sandbox Problem, Akshat Bubna, Modal CTO
